problem_text:
A certain municipality aims to devise a strategic intervention to curtail the aggregate discharge of a specific chemical effluent from a collection of industrial processing units. Presently, no mitigation procedures are in place.  

The operational profile for each unit is delineated as follows:  
* Unit A exhibits a discharge coefficient of 1.448 and a throughput of 191.464.  
* Unit B exhibits a discharge coefficient of 1.882 and a throughput of 264.49.  
* Unit C exhibits a discharge coefficient of 0.64 and a throughput of 73.84.  
* Unit D exhibits a discharge coefficient of 0.524 and a throughput of 182.04.  
* Unit E exhibits a discharge coefficient of 0.928 and a throughput of 60.638.  
* Unit F exhibits a discharge coefficient of 1.75 and a throughput of 102.854.  
* Unit G exhibits a discharge coefficient of 1.585 and a throughput of 267.029.  
* Unit H exhibits a discharge coefficient of 2.461 and a throughput of 271.889.  

A suite of purification technologies can be deployed, each associated with a distinct abatement efficacy:  
* Technology Alpha reduces effluent concentration by 52%.  
* Technology Beta reduces effluent concentration by 86%.  
* Technology Gamma reduces effluent concentration by 84%.  
* Technology Delta reduces effluent concentration by 16%.  
* Technology Epsilon reduces effluent concentration by 18%.  
* Technology Zeta reduces effluent concentration by 45%.  
* Technology Eta reduces effluent concentration by 87%.  
* Technology Theta reduces effluent concentration by 16%.  

Implementing a technology at a unit entails an incremental expenditure per unit of throughput. The cost matrix for all unit–technology pairings is provided:  

| Unit \ Technology | Alpha | Beta | Gamma | Delta | Epsilon | Zeta | Eta | Theta |
|--|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Unit A | 69.752 | 192.679 | 121.537 | 152.928 | 145.415 | 85.676 | 24.618 | 40.866 |
| Unit B | 55.69 | 168.584 | 83.94 | 180.34 | 73.029 | 153.566 | 36.591 | 197.811 |
| Unit C | 147.591 | 105.151 | 195.121 | 20.202 | 93.047 | 169.348 | 74.713 | 156.111 |
| Unit D | 191.423 | 85.374 | 156.975 | 15.629 | 61.932 | 198.591 | 103.215 | 77.604 |
| Unit E | 188.817 | 92.051 | 139.142 | 135.528 | 26.282 | 127.537 | 161.63 | 145.491 |
| Unit F | 25.587 | 39.302 | 145.219 | 130.441 | 150.535 | 70.169 | 30.245 | 10.987 |
| Unit G | 68.571 | 78.384 | 61.256 | 35.176 | 45.604 | 95.28 | 115.401 | 87.528 |
| Unit H | 14.99 | 77.244 | 27.682 | 123.628 | 71.642 | 83.195 | 65.451 | 83.682 |

The decision involves selecting which technologies to apply to each processing unit (units may adopt several technologies concurrently), and it is permissible for a unit to remain partially untreated. The objective is to guarantee that the total chemical effluent is diminished by at least a fraction P = 0.242 of the baseline discharge, while simultaneously minimizing the aggregate implementation cost.
